passages.text: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present.
Many people came near to Jesus.
All the tax collectors came near to Jesus.
All the sinners came near to Jesus.
They wanted to listen to Jesus.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες πάντες οἱ τελῶναι καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees and the scribes were religious leaders.
They began to grumble.
They said, “This man welcomes sinners.
He eats with them.”
passages.original: καὶ διεγόγγυζον οἵ τε Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ἁμαρτωλοὺς προσδέχεται καὶ συνεσθίει αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Then Jesus told them this parable: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them a parable.
Jesus said, "Suppose one of you has one hundred sheep.
You lose one sheep.
You still have ninety-nine sheep.
You leave the ninety-nine sheep in the open country.
You go after the one lost sheep.
You keep searching until you find it."
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγων Τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἔχων ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ ἀπολέσας ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν οὐ καταλείπει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ πορεύεται ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπολωλὸς ἕως εὕρῃ αὐτό

passages.text: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders, comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable about a man with one hundred sheep.
The man loses one sheep.
He searches for the lost sheep until he finds it.
When the man finds the lost sheep, he feels great joy.
He lifts the sheep onto his shoulders.
He carries the sheep home.
He arrives at his house.
He calls his friends and neighbors together.
He says to them, “Rejoice with me.”
He says, “I have found my lost sheep.”
passages.original: καὶ εὑρὼν ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους αὐτοῦ χαίρων καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον συνκαλεῖ τοὺς φίλους καὶ τοὺς γείτονας λέγων αὐτοῖς Συνχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὸ πρόβατόν μου τὸ ἀπολωλός

passages.text: In the same way, I tell you that there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus told them about God’s joy.
God lives in heaven.
God feels great joy when one sinner repents.
God feels more joy for one sinner who turns back to Him than for ninety-nine righteous people.
These ninety-nine righteous people do not need to repent.
passages.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως χαρὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἔσται ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι ἢ ἐπὶ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα δικαίοις οἵτινες οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν μετανοίας

passages.text: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?
passages.sermon:
A woman has ten silver coins.
She loses one coin.
She lights a lamp.
She sweeps her house.
She searches carefully.
She keeps searching until she finds the lost coin.
passages.original: Ἢ τίς γυνὴ δραχμὰς ἔχουσα δέκα ἐὰν ἀπολέσῃ δραχμὴν μίαν οὐχὶ ἅπτει λύχνον καὶ σαροῖ τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ζητεῖ ἐπιμελῶς ἕως οὗ εὕρῃ

passages.text: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors to say, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’
passages.sermon:
A woman had ten silver coins.
She lost one coin.
She searched carefully until she found it.
When she found the lost coin, she called her friends and neighbors.
She said, "Rejoice with me."
She said, "I have found the coin I lost."
passages.original: καὶ εὑροῦσα συνκαλεῖ τὰς φίλας καὶ γείτονας λέγουσα Συνχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα

passages.text: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He explained what happens in heaven.
God’s angels see everything.
When one sinner repents, the angels rejoice.
There is joy before God’s angels over one person who turns away from sin.
passages.original: οὕτως λέγω ὑμῖν γίνεται χαρὰ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι

passages.text: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them a story.
A man lived in the story.
This man had two sons.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δέ Ἄνθρωπός τις εἶχεν δύο υἱούς

passages.text: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.
passages.sermon:
A man had two sons.
The younger son spoke to his father.
He said, "Father, give me my share of the estate."
The father listened to his younger son.
The father divided his property between his two sons.
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ νεώτερος αὐτῶν τῷ πατρί Πάτερ δός μοι τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος τῆς οὐσίας ὁ δὲ διεῖλεν αὐτοῖς τὸν βίον

passages.text: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.
passages.sermon:
A man had two sons.
The younger son gathered all he had.
He left home after a few days.
He traveled to a distant country.
He spent all his wealth there.
He lived in a reckless and wasteful way.
passages.original: Καὶ μετ’ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας συναγαγὼν πάντα ὁ νεώτερος υἱὸς ἀπεδήμησεν εἰς χώραν μακράν καὶ ἐκεῖ διεσκόρπισεν τὴν οὐσίαν αὐτοῦ ζῶν ἀσώτως

passages.text: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.
passages.sermon: The younger son spent all his money.\r\nA severe famine struck that country.\r\nThe younger son began to lack what he needed.
passages.original: Δαπανήσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο λιμὸς ἰσχυρὰ κατὰ τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ αὐτὸς ἤρξατο ὑστερεῖσθαι

passages.text: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.
passages.sermon:
The younger son left home.
He traveled to a distant country.
He spent all his wealth.
A severe famine struck that country.
He became needy.
He went to a citizen of that country.
He hired himself out to that man.
The man sent him into his fields.
He told him to feed the pigs.
passages.original: καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐκολλήθη ἑνὶ τῶν πολιτῶν τῆς χώρας ἐκείνης καὶ ἔπεμψεν αὐτὸν εἰς τοὺς ἀγροὺς αὐτοῦ βόσκειν χοίρους

passages.text: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.
passages.sermon:
A young man had spent all his money.
A severe famine struck the country where he lived.
He became very hungry and needy.
He worked for a citizen of that country.
The man sent him to feed pigs in the fields.
He saw the pigs eating pods.
He wanted to fill his stomach with the pods the pigs were eating.
No one gave him anything to eat.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπεθύμει γεμίσαι τὴν κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν κερατίων ὧν ἤσθιον οἱ χοῖροι καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδίδου αὐτῷ

passages.text: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food? But here I am, starving to death!
passages.sermon:
A young man left his home.
He wasted all his money in a distant country.
He became very poor and hungry.
He worked for a man who sent him to feed pigs.
He wanted to eat the food the pigs ate, but no one gave him anything.
He realized his situation.
He said, “My father’s hired servants have plenty of bread.”
He said, “But I am dying here from hunger.”
passages.original: Εἰς ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἐλθὼν ἔφη Πόσοι μίσθιοι τοῦ πατρός μου περισσεύονται ἄρτων ἐγὼ δὲ λιμῷ ὧδε ἀπόλλυμαι

passages.text: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
passages.sermon:
A young man left his father and wasted all his money.
He became very hungry and poor.
He decided to return to his father.
He said, “I will get up now.
I will go to my father.
I will speak to him.
I will say, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven.
I have sinned against you.’”
passages.original: ἀναστὰς πορεύσομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ ἐρῶ αὐτῷ Πάτερ ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου

passages.text: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.” ’
passages.sermon: The son spoke to his father.\r\nHe said he was not worthy to be called his son.\r\nHe asked his father to make him like one of the hired servants.
passages.original: οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου ποίησόν με ὡς ἕνα τῶν μισθίων σου

passages.text: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.
passages.sermon:
A son left his home and sinned.
He decided to return to his father.
He got up and went to his father.
While the son was still far away, his father saw him.
The father felt deep compassion for his son.
The father ran to his son.
He embraced his son.
He kissed his son.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰς ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἑαυτοῦ ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος εἶδεν αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη καὶ δραμὼν ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν

passages.text: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
passages.sermon:
The son spoke to his father.
He said, “Father, I have sinned against heaven.
I have sinned against you.
I am not worthy to be called your son.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτῷ Πάτερ ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου

passages.text: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
passages.sermon:
The father saw his son return home.
The father felt compassion for his son.
The father spoke to his servants.
He said, “Quick! Bring the best robe.”
He told them, “Put the robe on my son.”
He said, “Put a ring on his finger.”
He said, “Put sandals on his feet.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ πρὸς τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ Ταχὺ ἐξενέγκατε στολὴν τὴν πρώτην καὶ ἐνδύσατε αὐτόν καὶ δότε δακτύλιον εἰς τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ὑποδήματα εἰς τοὺς πόδας

passages.text: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.
passages.sermon:
The father spoke to his servants.
He said, "Bring the fattened calf."
"Kill it."
"Let us eat together."
"Let us celebrate."
passages.original: καὶ φέρετε τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν θύσατε καὶ φαγόντες εὐφρανθῶμεν

passages.text: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.
passages.sermon:
The father spoke about his son.
The son had left home and lived far away.
The father said, "This son of mine was dead."
He meant the son was gone from his life.
The father said, "Now he is alive again."
He meant the son has returned home.
The father said, "He was lost."
He meant the son was separated from the family.
The father said, "Now he is found."
He meant the son is back with the family.
The people began to celebrate.
They rejoiced because the son returned.
passages.original: ὅτι οὗτος ὁ υἱός μου νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἀνέζησεν ἦν ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη καὶ ἤρξαντο εὐφραίνεσθαι

passages.text: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
passages.sermon:
The older son was in the field.
He was working there.
He started to come home.
He walked closer to the house.
He heard music.
He heard dancing.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ πρεσβύτερος ἐν ἀγρῷ καὶ ὡς ἐρχόμενος ἤγγισεν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἤκουσεν συμφωνίας καὶ χορῶν

passages.text: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
passages.sermon:
The older son stood near the house.
He did not know why there was music and dancing.
He called one of the servants to him.
He asked the servant, “What is happening?”
passages.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα τῶν παίδων ἐπυνθάνετο τί ἂν εἴη ταῦτα

passages.text: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’
passages.sermon:
A servant spoke to the older son.
He said, "Your brother has come home."
He said, "Your father has killed the fattened calf."
He said, "Your father did this because he received your brother back safe and sound."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἥκει καὶ ἔθυσεν ὁ πατήρ σου τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν ὅτι ὑγιαίνοντα αὐτὸν ἀπέλαβεν

passages.text: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
passages.sermon:
The older son became angry.
He refused to go in.
His father came out.
His father pleaded with him.
passages.original: Ὠργίσθη δὲ καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν εἰσελθεῖν ὁ δὲ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐξελθὼν παρεκάλει αὐτόν

passages.text: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
passages.sermon:
The older son spoke to his father.
He said, "Look at me."
I have served you for many years.
I have never disobeyed any of your commands.
You never gave me a young goat.
I wanted to celebrate with my friends.
You did not let me do this.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰδοὺ τοσαῦτα ἔτη δουλεύω σοι καὶ οὐδέποτε ἐντολήν σου παρῆλθον καὶ ἐμοὶ οὐδέποτε ἔδωκας ἔριφον ἵνα μετὰ τῶν φίλων μου εὐφρανθῶ

passages.text: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
passages.sermon:
The older son spoke to his father.
He said, “This son of yours wasted your wealth.
He spent your money on prostitutes.
He came back home.
You killed the fattened calf for him.”
passages.original: ὅτε δὲ ὁ υἱός σου οὗτος ὁ καταφαγών σου τὸν βίον μετὰ πορνῶν ἦλθεν ἔθυσας αὐτῷ τὸν σιτευτὸν μόσχον

passages.text: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.
passages.sermon: The father spoke to his older son.\r\nHe said, “Son, you are always with me.\r\nEverything I have belongs to you.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τέκνον σὺ πάντοτε μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἶ καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐμὰ σά ἐστιν

passages.text: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The father spoke to the older son.
The father said it was right to celebrate.
The father said it was right to be glad.
Your brother was dead.
Now your brother is alive again.
Your brother was lost.
Now your brother is found.
passages.original: εὐφρανθῆναι δὲ καὶ χαρῆναι ἔδει ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου οὗτος νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἔζησεν καὶ ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη
